reason: The argument-binding correction explicitly named result-binding as a separate, still-open TARGET: 'it needs enclosing-binding context threaded through the CALL walker's statement-level traversal, which argument binding did not need.' This record closes that TARGET.
core/src/semantic/call.rs's module doc comment already named 'argument/result bindings' together as part of the CallFact contract; only half was closed previously.

design_decision.question: Can result-binding reuse the exact same PlaceRef/identity_key-reuse mechanism argument-binding proved, or does it need new machinery?
design_decision.answer: Reuse, with one narrowing not needed for arguments: a call's return value only has a well-defined 'result' when the call expression IS THE ENTIRE value position, not a subexpression (`let y = helper(x) + 1;` has no single value the call's result 'becomes'), and only when the binding pattern is a single simple identifier, not a destructuring one (`let (a, b) = two_args_tuple(x, x);` -- a call's one return value has no defined mapping onto two separately-bound names, even though R4.12's own destructuring fix now binds both `a` and `b` for DATA_FLOW's own purposes).
design_decision.mechanism: core::semantic::call::CallSiteIdentity gained result: PlaceRef, excluded from identity_key() (same precedent as arguments/dispatch/callees). adapter::semantic::rust::mod's walk_stmt (Stmt::Local) and walk_expr (Expr::Assign) compute the result PlaceRef via the SAME place_ref_for_value helper argument-binding already uses (generalized to take a ValueRole parameter: Definition for let, Store for assignment), gated the same way (self.wants(DataFlow)) and recognized via spelling::simple_binding_ident (Pat::Ident/Pat::Type only -- deliberately narrower than dataflow.rs's own walk_binding_pat, which finds every identifier a destructuring pattern binds; result-binding needs 'is this ONE identifier', not 'find every identifier').
design_decision.threading_without_a_new_parameter: Rather than threading a 'result binding' parameter through the entire recursive walk_expr descent (which would touch every existing call site), a new walk_value_position_expr method intercepts ONLY at the exact two syntactic positions that can have a well-defined result (a Stmt::Local's direct init, an Expr::Assign's direct right-hand side): if the expression there is exactly Call/MethodCall, it calls the shared walk_call_like helper with the real computed result; otherwise it delegates to the ordinary walk_expr (implying Unresolved). walk_expr's own Call/MethodCall arms (reached from every other position) always pass PlaceRef::Unresolved via the same walk_call_like helper, so there is exactly one code path that ever emits a CALL observation, whichever way it was reached.

fix.what: CallSiteIdentity.result: PlaceRef. adapter::semantic::rust::mod's Stmt::Local and Expr::Assign handling compute it via place_ref_for_let_result/place_ref_for_assign_result and pass it through walk_value_position_expr/walk_call_like.

new_interpretation: R4.5's CALL<->DATA_FLOW binding gap (.atlas/contracts/SEMANTIC-FACTS.md#callfact's 'argument/result bindings') is now CLOSED in both halves. R4.5's overall closure status (macro-invocation-opacity gap, shared with every other full-expression-tree dimension) is otherwise unchanged.
required_runtime_invariants: a call that is the direct initializer of a simple let binding resolves to DATA_FLOW's own Definition record_id for that binding
a call that is the direct right-hand side of a simple assignment resolves to DATA_FLOW's own Store record_id
a call buried inside a larger expression never fabricates a result binding
a call whose enclosing pattern destructures stays Unresolved even though DATA_FLOW itself binds every sub-identifier
result is only ever Resolved when DataFlow was requested in the same extraction call
result never affects a call site's own identity_key()
